newsitem.title: USA: Gore invites Saudi Crown Prince to Washington.
newsitem.headline: Gore invites Saudi Crown Prince to Washington.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore on Friday invited Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Abdullah to visit Washington at a mutually convenient time.

The invitation was contained in a letter Gore gave to Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan at the end of a meeting at which they discussed the prince's visit to Washington this week, the vice president's office said.

Crown Prince Abdullah is first deputy prime minister of Saudi Arabia and was put in charge of running the Saudi government more than a year ago after his half-brother, King Fahd, suffered a stroke in November 1995.

Gore spokeswoman Lorraine Voles said Gore and Prince Sultan reaffirmed the strategic importance of Saudi Arabia in the world oil market "and its role as a secure, dependable and reliable oil exporter."
They also stressed the importance of cooperation in the fight against terrorism.
During his visit the prince renewed pledges of cooperation with the United States in the investigation of a truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. troops last June near Dhahran.
